newsitem.title: USA: Michigan says Ameritech can satisfy checklist.
newsitem.headline: Michigan says Ameritech can satisfy checklist.

text.p: Ameritech Corp has satisfied 11 of 14 items on a checklist of requirements to provide long-distance telephone service in Michigan, the Michigan Public Service Commission (MPSC) said Tuesday
MPSC said it believes the company can meet the other three requirements within the Federal Communications Commission's review period.

"We believe that improvements in the three areas we have noted can be accomplished in the remaining 70 days prior to FCC action on Ameritech's Michigan application," MPSC Chairman John Strand said in a statement.

Under the Telecommunications Act of 1996, Ameritech and other Baby Bells must satisfy a checklist proving they have opened their local phone markets to new competitors before they can provide long-distance service from their regions.
The FCC will make the final decision on whether Ameritech has met the checklist for entry into the lucrative market.

MPSC said before the FCC could make a determination, Ameritech must set standards that would give other carriers access to Ameritech's support services equal to the quality Ameritech provides to its own customers.
The commission also said the issue of shared transport with local exchange carriers remains unresolved, but could be settled based on the results of Ameritech trials.
MPSC said although Ameritech technically satisfied the checklist item on 911 emergency services and databases, Ameritech should improve the accuracy of its 911 records.

In February, MPSC voted to advise the FCC that Ameritech had met the checklist, but the Chicago-based Baby Bell was forced to withdraw that bid for long distance after the FCC noted Michigan had not approved the company's interconnection agreement with long-distance giant AT&T Corp.
Ameritech has pegged the long-distance market in its five-state region at $9 billion. It has said it hopes to offer the service in all of its five Midwestern states by the end of the year.
